_comment: WHICH PUBLISHED SPELLING MEANS WHICH LONG TRAIL. A reviewed join, in pipeline/reference/ rather than derived at build time, because deciding that OUACHITA NRT is the Ouachita Trail and that a NY State Parks line called 'Long Trail' is NOT Vermont's is a judgement somebody signs for, row by row. CONTRIBUTING.md's line ceiling applies for exactly that reason. WHY IT EXISTS. map/trailsInView.ts decided a badge off the SOURCE - `BADGE_SOURCES`, two entries - so the A.T. and the Long Path were the only trails on the map that could ever wear one, while Sheltowee Trace, Ozark Highlands, Bartram, Pinhoti, Ouachita, Maah Daah Hey and the rest were already drawn as anonymous lines. A trail is not a feed, and this file is what lets the badge key off the trail.
_method:
MEASURED 2026-09-30 against each layer's live service, in two steps. FIRST a name probe: every trail in trail_emblems.json, queried with LIKE on the publisher's own name field, then normalised on both sides - upper-cased, punctuation stripped, and the words TRAIL/NRT/NST/NATIONAL/SCENIC/RECREATION/HISTORIC/HIKING dropped - and kept only where the normalised forms were equal. That alone was not enough and produced confident nonsense, so SECOND a geographic check: every surviving candidate's extent was fetched and compared with the states trail_emblems.json records for that trail. The second step rejected 16 names the first step accepted, and they are listed in `rejected` below so nobody re-adds them.

EXTENDED 2026-09-30 FOR #1776, by a different check, because the pipeline now uses this table to decide which lines are one trail and not only which wear a badge. A spelling joins a trail when it appears in a RUN OF SHARED TREAD that totals at least NAMED_TRAIL_THRESHOLD_MILES and in which EVERY spelling names that trail. Continuity says it is one trail; the names say which. Neither alone is enough - names alone is what gave GREEN MOUNTAIN 27 unrelated trails in 27 national forests, and continuity alone folded ALLEGHENY TRAIL and GLENWOOD HORSE into the Appalachian Trail. Measured against release 2026-09-16-4's published nearby_trails.geojson, chaining on any shared vertex within 200 m. Roads, connectors, ties, accesses, spurs, approaches and motorized routes are excluded BY NAME first, as below - which is what keeps ANST - APPALACHIAN RD out at 159 miles, the single largest thing this check rejects.
_what_it_does_not_cover: Spurs, connectors and road-walks are not here even where the publisher names them after the trail - 'Northville-Placid Trail Spur', 'BARTRAM NRT - CHEOAH RD', 'Finger Lakes Trail Spur'. The match is exact against the spellings listed, never a prefix, so those stay ordinary lines. Three long trails turned up in these layers that trail_emblems.json does not carry - Shawangunk Ridge, Taconic Crest and Metacomet-Monadnock - and are recorded in trail_candidates.json rather than badged here.
_row_count: 19 trails with at least one verified spelling, across 3 published layers. #1776 added 94 usfs_trails spellings to four of them; the count of trails did not move.

at.note: Already badged through ATC's own `centerline` source; these are the USFS segments of the same trail, 165 and 4 respectively, in GA-VA and VT. #1776 added APPALACHIAN TRAIL/LONG TRAIL, the 111 miles USFS publishes for the Vermont concurrency where both trails share tread.

usfs_trails: PCT WRIGHT MT TO INSPIRATION P

pct.note: 37 + 5 + 2 segments, all between lon -123.3 and -118.0. #1776 added 78 more spellings, 1,800 miles across twelve runs of shared tread. The LARGEST of those runs - 424 miles through the Oregon and Washington Cascades, nine spellings - contained NO spelling this table already listed, which is why a check that needed one as a seed could not have found it.

cdt.note: Five spellings of one trail, 267 segments together, lon -113.9..-106.2 and lat 32.4..47.2 - the whole divide. #1776 added the CDNST spellings: eight more, 292 miles, every one in a run of shared tread that clears 50 miles and in which every spelling names this trail.

nct.note: 45 segments spanning lon -97.5..-78.8, which is ND to NY. #1776 added seven more, including the segment-numbered spellings (NORTH COUNTRY NATIONAL 383-187 and its five siblings) and NORTH COUNTRY NTL SCENIC-EAST.

azt.note: Both inside Arizona. 'ARIZONA TRAIL CANELO HILLS' and the AZT spur names are deliberately absent - they normalise differently and are sections.

flt.note: The one trail here three different organizations publish. Spur spellings are excluded.

sht.note: 28 segments at lon -91.0..-89.9, lat 47.5..47.9 - the north shore. Bare 'SUPERIOR' was rejected; see below.

ouachita.note: The Forest Service calls it by its National Recreation Trail designation and the association calls it the Ouachita Trail. 20 segments, lon -95.0..-92.8.

sheltowee.note: 64 segments, lon -84.7..-83.4, lat 36.6..38.4. The connector and spur spellings are excluded.

pinhoti.note: 3 segments in GA and 16 in AL.

bmt.note: 7 segments, lon -84.5..-84.1. The two road spellings are sections and are excluded.

bartram.note: 3 segments, lon -85.7..-83.2. The NRT road-section spellings are excluded.

mdh.note: 31 segments in the Little Missouri grassland.

bst.note: 26 segments along the Wasatch front. The NE/NORTH/SOUTH/SPUR spellings are sections and are excluded.

jmt.note: 4 segments at lon -119.2, lat 37.6 - Yosemite. 'JOHN MUIR NATIONAL RECREATION' was rejected: it is in Tennessee.

npt.note: DEC publishes the trail and five separate spur spellings; only the trail is here.

rejected.usfs_trails 'LONG' and 'LONG TRAIL': Vermont's Long Trail is not in the USFS layer. 'LONG' spans lon -115.5..-72.8 and 'LONG TRAIL' sits at lon -115.8 in Idaho. GMC's own data is the way in.
rejected.oprhp_trails 'Long Trail': lon -76.1, lat 43.0 - central New York, 200 miles from Vermont.
rejected.usfs_trails 'BUCKEYE': lon -121.4..-81.6, so California to Ohio under one name. Ohio's Buckeye Trail is not a Forest Service trail.
rejected.usfs_trails 'FOOTHILLS': lon -106.5..-83.0, New Mexico to South Carolina. 'BRIDGER FOOTHILLS' in Montana is one of them.
rejected.usfs_trails 'PALMETTO': one segment at lon -121.3, lat 39.8 - California.
rejected.usfs_trails 'CUMBERLAND': one segment at lon -106.5, lat 38.7 - Colorado. Tennessee's Cumberland Trail is a state park trail.
rejected.usfs_trails 'LONE STAR': lon -118.6..-95.1. Some of it is in Texas and some is not, and the Lone Star Hiking Trail is in Sam Houston National Forest only.
rejected.usfs_trails 'CATAMOUNT', dec_hiking_trai: Colorado, the Adirondacks and New Hampshire respectively. Vermont's Catamount Trail is in none of these layers.
rejected.usfs_trails 'BACKBONE' and 'BACKBONE TRA: country-wide and Arizona. California's Backbone Trail is in the Santa Monica Mountains NRA, which NPS administers.
rejected.usfs_trails 'BLACK CANYON' and 'BLACK CA: country-wide and Idaho. Arizona's Black Canyon Trail is BLM.
rejected.usfs_trails 'BAKER': lon -115.8..-109.0, Arizona and Utah. Pennsylvania's Baker Trail is not a Forest Service trail.
rejected.usfs_trails 'HOT SPRINGS' and 'HOT SPRIN: lon -115.2..-105.8. A common name for a common destination.
rejected.usfs_trails 'JOHN MUIR NATIONAL RECREATI: one segment at lon -84.5, lat 35.2 - Tennessee. A different John Muir trail.
rejected.usfs_trails 'SUPERIOR': two segments at lon -120.8..-111.3 - Nevada and Utah.
rejected.usfs_trails 'ARIZONA TRAIL CANELO HILLS': Sections and spurs of the Arizona Trail rather than the trail, and they normalise differently so they never matched; recorded so the distinction is on the record.
rejected.usfs_trails 'COLORADO': 90 segments in roughly the right part of Colorado, and it might be the Colorado Trail - UNRESOLVED, and left out because a wrong badge is worse than a missing one. This row used to cover 'CDNST - COLORADO' as well, on the grounds that it is the Continental Divide trail in Colorado and not the Colorado Trail. That was right, and #1776 acted on it: the spelling is now listed under `cdt`, where it belongs. Only the bare name is still unresolved.

_removed.msg — Monadnock-Sunapee Greenway, via nh: REMOVED 2026-09-30 because the layer went, not because the match was wrong. The maintainer removed NH GRANIT outright on 2026-09-28 (d53bd431, #1711): GRANIT describes its own layer as compiled 'for planning use only' with roads mixed in, republished with renamed columns without notice (#1646), and redrew 962 miles of USFS trails in the White Mountains. New Hampshire outside the national forest loses its trails with it, and the greenway is one of them. The spelling that matched was 'DUBLIN TRAIL MONADNOCK SUNAPEE GRNWY'. THE TEST CAUGHT THIS RATHER THAN A REVIEWER: test_every_spelling_is_published_by_a_source_this_app_draws went red in CI the moment this branch was merged against a main that had dropped the source.

_the_motorized_filter: RE-CHECKED 2026-09-30 after the same commit gave usfs_trails `excluded_when {terra_motorized: ['Y']}`, which drops 23,195 rows and 29,199 miles nationwide. Every spelling below was re-counted with and without the filter and NONE of them ships nothing: the Great Western Trail falls from 16 segments to 3 and the Continental Divide's NST spelling from 116 to 102, and the rest are unchanged. So the filter costs this table no rows - checked rather than assumed, because a spelling whose every segment was motorized would have been a badge that could never draw.
_what_1776_could_not_verify: Spellings that name one of these trails, are not a road or connector, and still did NOT land in a qualifying run of shared tread are left out and are NOT in `rejected` - they are unproven rather than refused. The largest are PCT: MT HOOD's neighbours where the Cascades run is cut, and NORTH COUNTRY NTL SCENIC -WEST at 24 miles. A publisher's gap and a wrong name look identical from here, and the weaker reading is the one this table takes.
